title: Rotations on the Coordinate Plane Core Test
description: Rotate points and figures about the origin, identify rotation rules, reason backward from images, and analyze rigid-motion properties.

questions.questionText: Point A is (2, 5). Rotate A 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin. What is A'?
questions.explanation: Use (x, y) -> (-y, x) for this rotation, so A' is (-5, 2).

questions.questionText: Point A is (-3, 4). Rotate A 90 degrees clockwise about the origin. What is A'?
questions.explanation: Use (x, y) -> (y, -x) for this rotation, so A' is (4, 3).

questions.questionText: Point A is (6, -1). Rotate A 180 degrees about the origin. What is A'?
questions.explanation: Use (x, y) -> (-x, -y) for this rotation, so A' is (-6, 1).

questions.questionText: Point A is (-5, -2). Rotate A 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin. What is A'?
questions.explanation: Use (x, y) -> (-y, x) for this rotation, so A' is (2, -5).

questions.questionText: Point A is (0, 7). Rotate A 90 degrees clockwise about the origin. What is A'?
questions.explanation: Use (x, y) -> (y, -x) for this rotation, so A' is (7, 0).

questions.questionText: Point A is (4, 0). Rotate A 180 degrees about the origin. What is A'?
questions.explanation: Use (x, y) -> (-x, -y) for this rotation, so A' is (-4, 0).

questions.questionText: Point A is (-6, 3). Rotate A 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin. What is A'?
questions.explanation: Use (x, y) -> (-y, x) for this rotation, so A' is (-3, -6).

questions.questionText: Point A is (1, -8). Rotate A 90 degrees clockwise about the origin. What is A'?
questions.explanation: Use (x, y) -> (y, -x) for this rotation, so A' is (-8, -1).

questions.questionText: Point A is (-2, -5). Rotate A 180 degrees about the origin. What is A'?
questions.explanation: Use (x, y) -> (-x, -y) for this rotation, so A' is (2, 5).

questions.questionText: Point A is (7, 2). Rotate A 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin. What is A'?
questions.explanation: Use (x, y) -> (-y, x) for this rotation, so A' is (-2, 7).

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule correctly rotates (3, -4) to (4, 3) about the origin?
questions.explanation: (3, -4) becomes (4, 3) when (x, y) -> (-y, x) is applied.

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule correctly rotates (-7, 1) to (1, 7) about the origin?
questions.explanation: (-7, 1) becomes (1, 7) when (x, y) -> (y, -x) is applied.

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule correctly rotates (5, 6) to (-5, -6) about the origin?
questions.explanation: (5, 6) becomes (-5, -6) when (x, y) -> (-x, -y) is applied.

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule correctly rotates (-4, -6) to (6, -4) about the origin?
questions.explanation: (-4, -6) becomes (6, -4) when (x, y) -> (-y, x) is applied.

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule correctly rotates (8, -3) to (-3, -8) about the origin?
questions.explanation: (8, -3) becomes (-3, -8) when (x, y) -> (y, -x) is applied.

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule correctly rotates (-1, 9) to (1, -9) about the origin?
questions.explanation: (-1, 9) becomes (1, -9) when (x, y) -> (-x, -y) is applied.

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule correctly rotates (6, 2) to (-2, 6) about the origin?
questions.explanation: (6, 2) becomes (-2, 6) when (x, y) -> (-y, x) is applied.

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule correctly rotates (-8, -5) to (-5, 8) about the origin?
questions.explanation: (-8, -5) becomes (-5, 8) when (x, y) -> (y, -x) is applied.

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule correctly rotates (2, -7) to (-2, 7) about the origin?
questions.explanation: (2, -7) becomes (-2, 7) when (x, y) -> (-x, -y) is applied.

questions.questionText: Triangle A(1, 2), B(4, 2), C(2, 5) is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin. Which list gives the image vertices?
questions.explanation: Rotate each vertex using (x, y) -> (-y, x) and keep the vertex order the same.

questions.questionText: Triangle P(-3, 1), Q(-1, 4), R(-5, 3) is rotated 90 degrees clockwise about the origin. Which list gives the image vertices?
questions.explanation: Rotate each vertex using (x, y) -> (y, -x) and keep the vertex order the same.

questions.questionText: Triangle D(2, -1), E(6, -1), F(4, -4) is rotated 180 degrees about the origin. Which list gives the image vertices?
questions.explanation: Rotate each vertex using (x, y) -> (-x, -y) and keep the vertex order the same.

questions.questionText: Triangle J(-2, -3), K(-6, -3), L(-3, -7) is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin. Which list gives the image vertices?
questions.explanation: Rotate each vertex using (x, y) -> (-y, x) and keep the vertex order the same.

questions.questionText: After a 90 degrees counterclockwise rotation about the origin, point P' is (-4, 3). What was the original point P?
questions.explanation: Undo the rotation. The preimage must rotate to (-4, 3), so P was (3, 4).

questions.questionText: After a 90 degrees clockwise rotation about the origin, point P' is (5, 2). What was the original point P?
questions.explanation: Undo the rotation. The preimage must rotate to (5, 2), so P was (-2, 5).

questions.questionText: After a 180 degrees rotation about the origin, point P' is (-6, 1). What was the original point P?
questions.explanation: Undo the rotation. The preimage must rotate to (-6, 1), so P was (6, -1).

questions.questionText: After a 90 degrees counterclockwise rotation about the origin, point P' is (7, -3). What was the original point P?
questions.explanation: Undo the rotation. The preimage must rotate to (7, -3), so P was (-3, -7).

questions.questionText: A point in Quadrant I is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin. Where must its image be?
questions.explanation: A rotation turns a point or figure around the center while preserving distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: A point in Quadrant II is rotated 90 degrees clockwise about the origin. Where must its image be?
questions.explanation: A rotation turns a point or figure around the center while preserving distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: A point in Quadrant III is rotated 180 degrees about the origin. Where must its image be?
questions.explanation: A rotation turns a point or figure around the center while preserving distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: A point in Quadrant IV is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin. Where must its image be?
questions.explanation: A rotation turns a point or figure around the center while preserving distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: Which statement is always true after a rotation about the origin?
options: Distances from the origin stay the same.
The x-coordinate always stays the same.
questions.correctAnswer: Distances from the origin stay the same.
questions.explanation: A rotation turns a point or figure around the center while preserving distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: Which property shows that rotations are rigid transformations?
options: The image is always in Quadrant I.
Corresponding side lengths and angles are preserved.
Every point keeps both original coordinates.
questions.correctAnswer: Corresponding side lengths and angles are preserved.
questions.explanation: A rotation turns a point or figure around the center while preserving distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: A point lies on the positive x-axis. After a 90 degree counterclockwise rotation about the origin, where does it land?
questions.explanation: A rotation turns a point or figure around the center while preserving distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: A point lies on the negative y-axis. After a 90 degree clockwise rotation about the origin, where does it land?
questions.explanation: A rotation turns a point or figure around the center while preserving distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: Point P(2, -7) is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise, then 180 degrees, both about the origin. Where is the final image point?
questions.explanation: First P becomes (7, 2). A 180 degree rotation sends that point to (-7, -2).

questions.questionText: Point P(-5, 3) is rotated 90 degrees clockwise, then 90 degrees clockwise again. What single rotation gives the same final image?
options: A 180 degree rotation about the origin
A 90 degree counterclockwise rotation about the origin
questions.correctAnswer: A 180 degree rotation about the origin
questions.explanation: Two quarter-turns in the same direction equal one half-turn.

questions.questionText: A triangle is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin. Vertex A moves from (4, 1) to (-1, 4). Which statement best justifies the move?
options: The x-coordinate stayed fixed and y changed sign.
The rule (x, y) -> (-y, x) sends (4, 1) to (-1, 4).
questions.correctAnswer: The rule (x, y) -> (-y, x) sends (4, 1) to (-1, 4).
questions.explanation: A 90 degree counterclockwise rotation changes (x, y) to (-y, x).

questions.questionText: Point M is 10 units from the origin. After any rotation about the origin, how far is M' from the origin?
questions.explanation: Rotations preserve distance from the center of rotation.

questions.questionText: A segment has endpoints A(1, 5) and B(6, 5). It is rotated 90 degrees clockwise about the origin. What must be true about A'B'?
options: A'B' is twice as long as AB.
A'B' has the same length as AB.
A'B' is half as long as AB.
questions.correctAnswer: A'B' has the same length as AB.
questions.explanation: A rotation is rigid, so it preserves the length of every segment.

questions.questionText: A student says a 90 degree clockwise rotation uses (x, y) -> (-y, x). What is the error?
options: That rule is for a 90 degree counterclockwise rotation.
That rule is for a translation.
That rule is for a 180 degree rotation.
questions.correctAnswer: That rule is for a 90 degree counterclockwise rotation.
questions.explanation: Clockwise and counterclockwise quarter-turns use inverse coordinate rules.

questions.questionText: Point N(-3, -8) is rotated to N'(8, -3). Which rotation was used?
questions.explanation: The rule (x, y) -> (-y, x) sends (-3, -8) to (8, -3).

questions.questionText: Point N(6, -4) is rotated to N'(-4, -6). Which rotation was used?
questions.explanation: The rule (x, y) -> (y, -x) sends (6, -4) to (-4, -6).

questions.questionText: Point N(-7, 2) is rotated to N'(7, -2). Which rotation was used?
options: Reflection across the line y = x
questions.explanation: A 180 degree rotation changes both coordinate signs.

questions.questionText: A square is rotated 90 degrees about the origin. Which measurement could change?
questions.explanation: A rotation changes location and direction, but not size or shape.

questions.questionText: After a rotation about the origin, P(0, 6) becomes P'(-6, 0). Which rotation matches this image?
questions.explanation: The positive y-axis turns to the negative x-axis under a 90 degree counterclockwise rotation.

questions.questionText: After a rotation about the origin, P(-9, 0) becomes P'(0, 9). Which rotation matches this image?
questions.explanation: The negative x-axis turns to the positive y-axis under a 90 degree clockwise rotation.

questions.questionText: A point is rotated 90 degrees clockwise, then 90 degrees counterclockwise, both about the origin. What is the final image?
questions.explanation: The two rotations undo each other because they are inverse moves.

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC is rotated 180 degrees about the origin. A side from A to B was 7 units long before the rotation. How long is A'B'?
options: It cannot be known without graphing.
questions.explanation: Rotations preserve lengths, so corresponding sides remain congruent.

questions.questionText: A figure is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin, then 90 degrees counterclockwise again. Which coordinate rule describes the combined move?
questions.explanation: Two 90 degree counterclockwise rotations make a 180 degree rotation.
